findings: Both captures describe a client-side Radar Session snapshot of browser/device signals for self/third-party tokenization or server-side card submission where these details are not automatically collected. Preferred Stripe integrations already send sufficient information; the Radar Session client still loads Stripe.js on web or uses supported mobile SDKs (iOS 21.6.0+, Android 16.9.0+).

Client creates a session late in checkout or while saving card details and passes the ID to the merchant server; continue on client error is typical guidance. The server attaches via radar_options.session. On-session dual attachment is recommended for comparing save-time and payment-time signals; PaymentIntent Create must attempt a charge with confirm=true. An existing Intent can receive the ID on its separate Confirm request. Off-session uses PaymentMethod creation and carries its associated client data to subsequent payments.

The guide says to verify attachment in the API response or by GET on PaymentIntent or PaymentMethod. This check is documentation for attachment, not proof a payment succeeds or that the fraud model acted on it.

The related November API labels allowed_payment_method_types optional and payment_method_types a computed response field; the exact-version changelog supplies separate authority for rejecting the old writable input.
